name: Executive order of September 9, 1873 fixing the northern boundary of the Swinomish Reservation (Treaty of Point Elliott)
promises: The Treaty of Point Elliott of January 22, 1855 reserved the peninsula at the southeast end of Perry's Island, called Shais-quihl, for the Swinomish; Royce records that this order fixed its northern boundary 'to render more certain the indefinite language of the treaty'.
The order sets the northern line from low-water mark on Similk Bay, along surveyed section lines in township 34 north, range 2 east, to low-water mark on Padilla Bay.

breaches.what: Swinomish Chairman Brian Cladoosby said the reservation boundaries promised by the 1855 treaty were changed by an executive order in 1873 that President Grant lacked authority to make, and that the tribe has contested it since 1873.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Swinomish Chairman Brian Cladoosby, as reported by Indianz.com from The Anacortes American

source.title: Swinomish Tribe seeks recognition of original reservation boundaries

today: Indianz.com reported in December 2016 that the Swinomish Tribe was asking for recognition of the reservation boundary it says the 1855 treaty promised, and that the request was contested locally. No court or Indian Claims Commission finding on the 1873 order was located.

nationVoice.summary: Through its chairman, the Tribe says the 1873 order changed the boundaries the 1855 treaty set and that the President had no authority to do so.

Swinomish Tribe seeks recognition of original reservation boundaries

openQuestions: Audit 2026-11-08: this record was first researched as the Port Madison (Suquamish) reservation. Royce's 1873 schedule (p. 864) and the order's own text show the September 9, 1873 order fixed the northern boundary of the Swinomish reservation; Royce lists the parties as 'Dwamish and others', the Point Elliott signatories. The Suquamish allotment-loss statement was removed because it concerns Port Madison, not this order.
The Samish Indian Nation and local governments say the 1873 line is the legal boundary and that federal courts have ruled against the Swinomish on it; those rulings were not opened.
The Swinomish Tribe's own published account was not reached (its site returned a bot challenge); the tribal position is taken from a news report quoting its chairman.
No Indian Claims Commission decision on this order was located; the Commission's Swinomish case concerns the Point Elliott cession.

plain.promised: The 1855 Point Elliott treaty reserved a peninsula on Perry's Island for the Swinomish. An 1873 order fixed the reservation's northern boundary to make the treaty's wording more certain.
plain.happened: The Swinomish chairman says the 1873 order changed the boundary the treaty promised and that the President had no power to do it. No court or commission finding was located.
plain.today: In 2016 the Swinomish asked for recognition of the boundary they say the treaty set; the request was contested.
